class_guess: Bell eats counter (SOMDCv6 TM7 + a '+1 pass at each 110 entered')
summary: SOMDCv6 TM7 + one change: A1=0RF runs a +1 pass each time a 110 digit is entered. Fits 208/208 sweeps.
mechanism: Tape: wall 11, then 3-cell digits L=110, 0=000, 1=100: a long run of L's, then a short counter.
Each sweep: the eater turns digits white until it reads a 1-digit; then k drain passes rebuild L's (k = digits eaten).
Only change vs SOMDCv6 TM7: each L entered (by eater or drain pass) first fires a +1 pass on the digits to its right.

rules.name: Sweep
rules.cases: r over L=110,0=000,1=100. Eater, k=0: 0->L,k+1 | L->L,k+1,+1 rest* | 1->L, count mode. Count mode k>=1: L->L, eater again, +1 rest* | 1->L,k-1 | 0->0,(k-1)/2 if k odd; 0->1,(k-2)/2 if even. Right end: k=0->1; odd->0; even->1; repeat. *=new vs TM7

rules.name: Eater enters L (new)
rules.steps: 6j+13 (j = digits before the first 000 in X)
rules.cases: A1 fires here. inc = +1 on the 0/1 digits, little-endian, L skipped; overflow appends 100. TM7: 1 D> 110 X -> 1 111 D> X in 11 steps (no pass)

rules.name: Drain pass enters L (new)
rules.cases: A1 fires here and the eater restarts after the L (115 of 208 sweeps to 1e9). TM7: B> 1 110 X -> 1 111 D> X in 10 steps (no pass)

template.module: TM7 (line 1626); TM8 (line 1874) has the identical proof
template.note:
Config S(r)=0^inf 11 D> r and digits 110/000/100 carry over (no other digit to 1e9).
TM7's RIncs map fits 1/208 sweeps; with '+1 to the rest at every L entered' (eater and drain clause) it fits 208/208; eater clause alone: 95/208.

strategy:
Copy SOMDCv6 TM7 (S', ld/d0/d1, h/h', RIncs, BigStep, nonhalt). Add Inductive Inc (+1, L skipped) proved as one h-pass,
sideRLs tm [h] (toRC r) (toRC r') (BC-style: B>000-><C100, B>100->000B>, 110<->011). Insert Inc into RIncs_hx_ld and RIncs_h1_ld,
redo RIncs_nxt, then nonhalt via multistep_nonhalt + progress_nonhalt_cond exactly as TM7.
risks: Domain lemma (TM7's RIncs_nxt) must absorb the extra +1s; in the abstract run the pass count k in count mode gets as low as 1.
+1 can lengthen the word (overflow appends 100), so RIncs_nxt's induction on r gets more cases.
Twin 1RB0RA_... (A1=0RA, also open) uses extra digits 010/011/111: own rules, no free second kill.
